# serverroom_server_os (Resource)

The operating system on a dedicated server. Changing `os` (or `ssh_keys` / `user_data`) REINSTALLS the server and erases its disks -- only when `allow_reinstall = true`. Creating this resource for a server already running `os` adopts it without touching it; destroying it leaves the server as it is.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Adopts the running system as it is. Changing os, ssh_keys or user_data later
# REINSTALLS the server and erases its disks, and only with allow_reinstall = true.
resource "serverroom_server_os" "web" {
  account_id      = 246447
  os              = "Ubuntu 24.04"
  ssh_keys        = file("~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub")
  user_data       = file("${path.module}/cloud-init.yaml")
  allow_reinstall = false
  wait            = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `account_id` (Number) The server's service id (data.serverroom_servers).
- `os` (String) Exactly as sold for the plan, e.g. "Ubuntu 24.04".

### Optional

- `allow_reinstall` (Boolean) Must be true for a change to reinstall the server.
- `ssh_keys` (String) OpenSSH public keys for root, one per line (Linux).
- `user_data` (String, Sensitive) #cloud-config (Ubuntu) or a #! script, run once after the install.
- `wait` (Boolean) Wait (up to 90 minutes) until the reinstall is done and the server is back, so what depends on it runs against the new system.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
